## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D1 (b, clinical components). This is audit backlog UX-21 of the Nov 2026 product UX audit (an audit id, not an MDV key).

Persona and route: Components only, in /__ui. Later every status label in every role.
Findings and reviewers: F-19, F-20 · reviewers B-08, C-04, C-21. Part 2 of 3 of audit backlog UX-21 (part 1 is the tone tokens; part 3 replaces the local chips in features, after the pilot).
Rationale: About 12 chip variants exist; three styles sit side by side on one Today row. One vocabulary with tones removes the drift and gives the allergy one presentation.
Proposed UX behaviour: Chip (rounded, for a state: tone, optional icon, two sizes), Tag (square, for a category or source, such as from nurse intake) and Banner (a full-width notice with tone, icon, title, text and one optional action) in packages/ui, all taking the tone names of the token layer. Every one carries a text label; an icon may be added, colour never stands alone. The existing FrontDeskTag, StatusChip and ProvenanceTag become thin wrappers over them with unchanged looks. The allergy presentation used by PatientBanner is exported as AllergyBlock so the chart, the consultation and the dialogs share it. The ai tone is violet and dashed with the word draft and is never used for anything a clinician accepted.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/08-design-system-blueprint.md sections 6 and 7; docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html, audit notes 2 and 5.
Components and tokens affected: New chip.tsx, tag.tsx, banner.tsx in packages/ui; primitives.tsx wrappers. Tone tokens.
Front end and back end split: Front end only.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the tone-token ticket. File ownership in wave D1b: its three files; it edits primitives.tsx only to wrap the three existing primitives, after the tone-token ticket has merged.
Clinical sign-off: Required before merge for the allergy look only: question 4 of the validation plan. The other chips keep their looks.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low: wrappers keep today's looks; the comparison of the gallery proves it.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Replacing the local chips in features (after the pilot). (2) Changing any status wording.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given /__ui, when Chip, Tag and Banner are opened, then each renders in the seven tones, with and without an icon, in English and Arabic
- [ ] **AC2.** Given FrontDeskTag, StatusChip and ProvenanceTag, when captured before and after, then no pixel differs
- [ ] **AC3.** Given any Chip, Tag or Banner, when it is built without a text label, then TypeScript fails the build
- [ ] **AC4.** Given AllergyBlock, when it renders recorded, not recorded and no known allergies, then the three match the presentation the pilot doctor agreed and the same component is used by PatientBanner
- [ ] **AC5.** Given the ai tone, when it renders, then it is dashed, carries the word draft and cannot be combined with a confirmed or signed label
- [ ] **AC6.** Given the gallery in English and Arabic, when axe runs, then there is no violation and text contrast is at least 4.5:1 for every tone

## Test notes

- Vitest: label required, tone mapping.
- Playwright on /__ui: capture comparison for the three wrappers; axe in en and ar.

## Notes / open questions
